area: AUDIT: game feel and other problems (combat readability, parry timing, AI fairness, camera, hit feedback, audio, lighting, death/retry loop, tutorials, input, performance)
summary:
The parry is close to impossible for a human to time. I traced it to four causes that stack, and all four can be measured.
(1) TIMING CUE TOO LATE. The only "incoming" cue is BladeGlint plus the swing sfx (Enemy.cs:461-466). It fires at stepNorm >= activeStart - 0.18, which is a fraction of the clip, not seconds. I simulated Enemy.TickAttack with the real clip lengths. The cue arrives 0.10-0.20 s before impact for every common attack: ninja a1 0.20 s, a2 0.12, a3 0.15, elite a2 0.10, sumo slaps 0.12/0.18, Mizuchi a2 0.10. Human visual reaction is about 0.25 s, so a player who reacts to the cue presses after the hit (chart telegraph_lead.png). The flash itself is a 0.9 m white sprite that lives 0.09 s (FXManager.cs:49, 231-234). The whoosh peaks 0.13 s after it starts, so it lands on the impact rather than before it. Also, a bug in the telegraph "hold" eats most of the designed pause: ninja a1 0.12 → 0.05 s real, Gorō slam 0.30 → 0.07, Gorō c1 0.20 → 0.12, Mizuchi a1 0.08 → 0.02. holdEnd (Enemy.cs:448) assumes the windup plays at speed 1, but the Snappy curve plays it at 0.85.
(2) THE BODIES CAN'T BE SEEN. In-game combat shots average 16-50/255 luminance, and 43-87% of pixels sit below 25/255 (finisher_prompt.png 16/255, boss_ozeki1 16/255). Black-clad ninjas on dark ground disappear entirely. A shadow-lift of the same frame shows three ninjas stacked on top of each other (darkness_lift_demo.png). Contributing factors: ACES tonemapping, contrast +12, vignette 0.28, near-black ExpSq fog (forest 0.022), BlackFloor 0.13, and no rim or key light on the characters. At the gameplay camera a ninja is about 88 px tall at 1080p and the blade is 2-3 px wide.
(3) THE WINDUPS DON'T READ. In the contact sheets, ninja attacks move only an arm and a thin blade. Sumo Attack1/Attack2 show almost no visible motion from the game camera. Guard and Exhausted poses have the same silhouette as idle.
(4) NO WAY TO LEARN. A mistimed parry gives no feedback and costs full damage. A legitimate whiff also shrinks the next parry window to 0.13 s through the spam penalty. On top of that, the AutoPilot "validated" parries with zero reaction time on StrikeEta <= 0.18 (AutoPilot.cs:133), which hid all of this.

Beyond the parry, the core loop is degenerate and feels passive. One parry exhausts a common enemy, and any exhausted common can be executed at full HP (Enemy.cs:178) through a ~2.6 s cinematic, so the best play is parry → F → watch. Meanwhile the player's offense keeps bouncing. poiseHits=2 means the third hit of Kaito's combo is always deflected and countered on a fresh ninja. Exhaustion consumes 1 imbalance per hit (Enemy.cs:633), so after a single parry the second combo hit hits Guard and gets countered. Every common windup can also be interrupted by mashing, and enemies track until impact, so side-stepping doesn't work.

Other self-critical findings:
- Combat camera: lock-on zooms in to 17 m, closer than exploration, and yaws ±9°, which rotates the controls. FOV "punches" are instant 8-23% zoom pops. There are no off-screen threat indicators.
- Audio: the AudioListener sits on the camera ~24 m away. SwordSwing.wav (-22 dBFS) is shared between Kaito's and the enemies' swing pools. Hit-stop and slow-mo pitch the parry sound down to 0.55-0.69. Every sfx is at volume 1.0.
- Unblockables must be dashed, but the dash costs 15 Spirit, so some attacks have no answer.
- Group AI: enemies clump, tokens are only 0.6 s apart, the Counter ignores tokens, and Kaito is vulnerable the instant the finisher cinematic ends.
- Bosses: a phase change makes the boss untargetable (lock-on drops), silently ignores hits and wipes imbalance. Bosses have no posture UI.
- Retry loop: ~6.4 s death sequence, plus a 75-91 m runback to Ōzeki/Mizuchi, plus an unskippable intro on every attempt.
- Slow-motion is overused.
- The tutorial freezes at T-0.18 s, so it teaches a cue the player can't see at full speed.
- Smaller items: input-buffer drops, lock-on taps that do nothing, and per-event GameObject/material allocations.

The plan below fixes the cue in code first; it is independent of the animation rework and has the highest return. Then come visibility, the loop rules, camera, audio, the retry loop and tutorials, each with concrete files and values.

issues.title: Parry cue arrives 0.10-0.20 s before impact (below human reaction time) and the telegraph 'hold' is eaten by a bug
issues.evidence:
Enemies/Enemy.cs:461 fires BladeGlint and the swing sfx at `stepNorm >= a.activeStart - 0.18f`. That is 18% of the clip, not a time. I simulated it (scratch sim_telegraph.py) with the real clip lengths from clips/index.txt and the Snappy(0.85,1.35,aStart,1) curve (EnemyArchetypes.cs:151).

Cue lead before impact:
- ninja Attack1: 0.200 s
- ninja Attack2: 0.117 s
- ninja Attack3: 0.150 s
- elite a2: 0.100 s
- sumo slap1: 0.117 s; slap2: 0.183 s; stomp: 0.25 s
- Gorō c3: 0.167 s
- Mizuchi a2: 0.100 s

Parry window is 0.24 s with a 0.11 s perfect window (PlayerConfig.cs:51-52). Reaction time is about 0.25 s, so a press made in response to the cue lands after the hit (telegraph_lead.png).

The glint is flashWhite ×0.5 = 0.9 m and lives 0.09 s (FXManager.cs:49, 233). enemy_swing_1.wav onsets at 0.07 s and peaks at 0.13 s, i.e. on the impact.

Hold bug: Enemy.cs:448 `holdEnd = telegraph + (activeStart-0.12)*stepLen` assumes the windup plays at speed 1.0, but the curve plays it at 0.85. Real holds vs designed:
- ninja a1: 0.12 → 0.05 s
- Mizuchi a1: 0.08 → 0.017 s
- Gorō c1: 0.20 → 0.117 s
- Gorō slam: 0.30 → 0.067 s

AboutToStrike/StrikeWarning = 0.18 (Enemy.cs:42-48) builds the same late timing into the tutorial.
issues.fix:
Make the tell time-based. In TickAttack, strikeEta is already computed (Enemy.cs:453). Fire the tell when `strikeEta <= a.cueLead`:
- New AttackDef.cueLead, defaults by kind: Light 0.45 s, Heavy 0.55 s, combo follow-up steps 0.40 s, Unblockable = whole windup (≥0.6 s).
- In BeginStep, if the natural windup is shorter than cueLead + 0.1 s, add telegraph hold so that cue→impact is constant per class.
- Move the whoosh to strikeEta <= 0.12 so its peak lands on the impact.

Fix the hold: store holdStart when stepNorm first crosses activeStart-0.12, and use `holding = telegraph>0 && stepNorm>=activeStart-0.12 && stateTime-holdStart < telegraph`. Mirror the same logic in EstimateStrikeEta.

New FXManager.ParryTell(Enemy, kind), all within the 0.45 s:
- whole-body rim flash: gold = parryable, red = unblockable, 0.15 s
- eye/head glint sprite, 0.6 m, 0.25 s
- shrinking ground ring under Kaito aimed at the attacker, 2.2 → 0.6 m over cueLead, closing exactly at impact

BladeGlint lifetime 0.09 → 0.2 s, size ×2. New sfx tell_parry (bright metallic ring, 80 ms attack) and tell_heavy, spatialBlend 0.3.

issues.title: Combat is unreadable in the dark: black ninjas vanish, frames are crushed
issues.evidence:
Luminance of screenshots (mean/255, % pixels <25):
- finisher_prompt.png: 16.5, 72%
- boss_ozeki1.png: 16.1, 87%
- boss_ozeki2.png: 27.7, 72%
- zone_cp_bamboo.png: 21.4, 69%
- intro_fight2.png: 25.6, 72%
- boss_mizuchi4/5: ~26, 70%

In finisher_prompt.png the three ninjas are invisible; only their HP bars show. The gamma-lifted copy (darkness_lift_demo.png) shows they are there.

Causes:
- ScreenFX.cs:47 ACES tonemapping, BaseContrast 12 (line 32), vignette 0.28 (line 30), postExposure 0.15 (line 66)
- ExponentialSquared fog toward near-black: bosque 0.022 with fogColor (0.04,0.07,0.08) (StoryText.cs:54), bambu 0.018 (StoryText.cs:84). With the camera 24-31 m away that is 17-24% fog on the gameplay plane.
- moon intensity 1.05 (WorldBuilder.cs:559)
- CharacterFactory.BlackFloor = 0.13 (CharacterFactory.cs:25)
- no rim/outline or player key light

Character size on screen: a ninja is ~88 px tall at 1080p (24 m, FOV 30, pitch 52 → 84 px/m × 1.7 m × cos52). The blade is 2-3 px wide.
issues.fix:
Post (ScreenFX.Awake/Update):
- Tonemapping Neutral, or keep ACES with postExposure 0.15 → 0.55
- contrast 12 → 4
- vignette 0.28 → 0.18 (0.12 in combat)
- add ShadowsMidtonesHighlights with shadows lifted (≈+0.06, slightly blue)

Fog (WorldBuilder.SetAtmosphere / StoryText.ConfigureZone): switch to Linear with start ≈ camera distance − 2 (≈20 m) and end +45 m, so the gameplay plane is never fogged. Or lower densities: bosque 0.022 → 0.011, bambu 0.018 → 0.011, muralla 0.016 → 0.011. Raise fogColor brightness ~+0.04.

Player 'moon lantern' (CharacterFactory.BuildPlayer): child point light at (0, 3.2, -0.6), range 8, intensity 1.4 (1.8 when CombatDirector.InCombat), color (0.72,0.82,1), no shadows, ForcePixel.

Character readability: URP Renderer Feature (Render Objects) on layers Player/Enemy:
- inverted-hull outline ≈0.015 m, dark navy (0.05,0.07,0.12)
- Shader Graph fresnel rim (power 3, intensity 0.5; enemies cold blue, Kaito warm)

BlackFloor 0.13 → 0.2 with a navy hue (0.10,0.12,0.20), coordinated with the model/variant work.

issues.title: Enemy windups and combat states are not readable at gameplay distance (animation cause of the parry problem)
issues.evidence:
Contact sheets (game-camera row):
- ninja_Attack1/2/3.png: the body never changes silhouette. Only one arm and a 2-3 px blade move. No crouch, lean or raised guard.
- sumo_Attack1.png and sumo_Attack2.png: essentially no visible motion across 8 frames, yet they are 18-20 damage heavies.
- ninja_Guard.png and ninja_Exhausted.png: the same silhouette as idle (guard = sword vertical; exhausted = no slump).

The only way to tell Guard (hitting it gets you countered) from Exhausted (free hits) is UI text ('防' / '¡DESEQUILIBRADO!', UIManager.cs:323).

Parry recoil uses the same 'Hit' clip as being struck (animParried='Hit', EnemyArchetypes.cs:183/222).
issues.fix:
For the animation team, as acceptance criteria per attack:
- anticipation ≥0.30 s with a whole-body pose change visible from 52° pitch: weapon raised above the head or pulled back behind the hip, torso twist ≥30°, knees bent
- hold 0.08-0.12 s, then a fast strike (≤0.1 s) and follow-through
- distinct Guard (blade raised, wide stance) and Exhausted (slumped, dizzy sway) poses
- a distinct parried recoil (weapon knocked back, step back)

Stop-gap in code, independent of the clips, using the same rim shader:
- Guard = steady blue rim plus a blade-up glint every 0.6 s
- Exhausted = pulsing gold rim plus orbiting 'dizzy' sparks
- Tell = 0.15 s full-body flash (GF-01)

Drive the ninja eye material emission (orange eyes already exist) from 0 to 4 during the tell.

issues.title: Failing a parry teaches nothing and is over-punished (full damage, spam penalty after legitimate attempts, 0.12 s buffer)
issues.evidence:
PlayerController.cs:400-430 ReceiveHit: a hit during ParryRecover or Parry outside the window is full damage plus Hurt 0.38-0.65 s. There is no early/late feedback.

PlayerController.Combat.cs:219/233: any parry that whiffs because the swing missed or was out of range sets lastParryWhiff. The next parry within 0.55 s then gets window ×0.55, i.e. 0.13 s (perfect 0.06 s). With a ninja a1 → a2 gap of ~0.57 s, a legitimate attempt on a1 nerfs the parry for a2.

Parry is buffered for only 0.12 s (PlayerController.cs:195, Combat.cs:84 0.1 s). Kaito's attack lock spans 0.085-0.238 s for Attack1 and 0.093-0.40 s for Attack3, so a parry pressed early in that span is silently dropped.

ParryStance clip is 0.1 s, the body doesn't change (kaito_ParryStance.png), and there is no whiff sound or animation.
issues.fix:
Add an 'imperfect guard' fallback in ReceiveHit: if State==ParryRecover && stateTime < 0.15 && info.CanBeParried, then:
- 35% damage, Push 0.4 m, no Hurt state
- clang sfx
- enemy +0.34 imbalance

Add learning feedback: if a hit lands ≤0.25 s after the parry window closed, show a small 'TEMPRANO' over Kaito. If the player presses parry ≤0.2 s after being hit, show 'TARDE'. Enable in the first two zones or as an option.

Spam penalty: apply only if no enemy within 6 m had StrikeEta < 0.6 s at press time. spamPenalty 0.55 → 0.75, decay 0.55 → 0.35 s.

Parry buffer 0.12 → 0.20 s everywhere (TryCombatActions, TickAttack, TickBlocked, TickParrySuccess, TickDash).

Add a short whiff 'swish' and a visible ParryStance (blade crossed in front, 0.24 s hold).

issues.title: Core loop is degenerate and passive: one parry → execute at full HP; the player's combos get bounced
issues.evidence:
Enemy.cs:178: CanBeFinished is true for ANY Exhausted common enemy regardless of HP. One parry leaves imbalance ≥1, so at ComboEnd the enemy becomes Exhausted (Enemy.cs:560) and is executable for 30 Spirit. The finisher is a ~2.6 s real-time cinematic: slow-mo 0.45 for 1.6 s (Combat.cs:400), strike at n=0.68 of a 2.667/1.7 s clip, plus hit-stop 0.16.

Offense is punished:
- poiseHits=2 (EnemyArchetypes.cs:181, Enemy.cs:621): the 3rd hit of Kaito's 3-hit combo on a neutral ninja is always 'Guarded' → Counter → Kaito Blocked. The elite (poise 1) bounces the 2nd hit.
- Hits on an Exhausted enemy consume ≥1 imbalance each (Enemy.cs:633). After a single parry, hit 1 ends exhaustion → EnterGuard, and hit 2 is countered.

The 'DESEQUILIBRADO' payoff is therefore one hit, unless you spend Spirit on the cinematic.
issues.fix:
- CanBeFinished for non-bosses: require Imbalance >= maxImbalance (posture broken) || Health01 <= 0.25. Partial exhaustion becomes a damage window only.
- Exhausted: stop consuming imbalance per hit. Exhaustion ends after exhaustedTime (3.2 → 2.4 s) or after 4 hits, then the enemy goes to Guard.
- First hit into Guard returns a clang plus a 0.3 m push with NO counter. Counter only on a 2nd hit within the same guard, and blocked hits add +0.25 imbalance (progress, like Sekiro posture).
- poiseHits: ninja 2 → 3, elite 1 → 2.
- Short finisher for commons: Play('Finisher', speed 2.6), no camera shot, slow-mo 0.6 for 0.35 s, ≤1.0 s total. Keep the cinematic for elites, the last enemy of an encounter, and bosses.

issues.title: Mashing beats parrying, and lateral dodges are impossible (no commit armor, tracking until impact)
issues.evidence:
Enemy.cs:652: only hyperArmor configs (sumo/Gorō) ignore hits during Attack. Every ninja, elite, Mizuchi and Kage attack is interrupted into Stagger by any hit (Enemy.cs:656-661). Kaito's Attack1 connects at 0.12 s while ninja windups are 0.30-0.60 s (sim), so attacking first always wins and the parry system is optional.

Enemy.cs:458: with tracking=true (default, CombatTypes.cs AttackDef), enemies rotate toward Kaito at turnSpeed×1.3 (=13, about 95% in 0.23 s) until activeStart. Side-stepping a committed swing never works.
issues.fix:
Commit armor: in TickAttack set `armored = strikeEta <= 0.30f`. In ReceiveHit, if Attack && armored && kind==Light, apply damage and HitFlash but no stagger and no token release. Heavy, Ability and riposte hits still interrupt.

Tracking: stop Face() when strikeEta < 0.20 s (time-based), so a last-moment side-step or walk-out is a valid read.

issues.title: Audio undermines combat reading: far listener, shared or silent swing clip, slow-mo pitching the parry, flat mix
issues.evidence:
CameraDirector.cs:72 puts the AudioListener on the camera, 24-31 m from the action. Sfx use linear rolloff min 4 / max 45 with spatialBlend 0.75 (AudioManager.cs:53, 214), so gameplay sounds play at ~0.5-0.6 of nominal and jump ~+60% in close cinematic shots.

NindoContent.asset sfx: Assets/Audios/SwordSwing.wav (peak -22 dBFS, ~20 dB quieter than the rest) sits in all three pools: 'swing' (Kaito), 'enemy_swing' and 'enemy_swing_heavy'. One enemy cue in 4 is nearly silent and sounds like Kaito's own swing.

AudioManager.cs:186-187 pitches every playing sfx by lerp(0.55,1,timeScale). Hit-stop sets timeScale 0, so the parry clang plays at 0.55 pitch for its first 70-110 ms, and the perfect parry's 0.3 slow-mo gives ≈0.69.

Mix: every one of the 48 sfx keys is at volume 1.0 and normalized to -1 dBFS. danger_1.wav has 0.41 s of leading silence. parry_perfect_1.wav is 4.6 s long.
issues.fix:
Listener: a child 'Listener' that follows Kaito's position +1.2 m with the camera's rotation. Sfx minDistance 4 → 6, maxDistance 45 → 35.

Swing pools: remove SwordSwing.wav from all three. Make enemy swings timbrally distinct (lower, cloth plus steel) and add the new tell_parry / tell_heavy (GF-01).

Pitch: exclude a no-pitch set (parry, parry_perfect, clang, hit, hit_heavy, tell_*, danger) from slow-mo pitch, and compute pitch from the slow-mo scale only, ignoring hit-stop.

Mix tiers: tells/danger 1.0, parry 1.0, hits 0.85, enemy swings 0.6, Kaito swings 0.5, footsteps call 0.35, ambience 0.4.

Trim danger_1.wav's leading 0.4 s and cut parry_perfect to ~2 s.

issues.title: Combat camera fights readability: lock-on zooms in and rotates the controls, FOV pops, no off-screen threats, occlusion only for Kaito
issues.evidence:
CameraDirector.cs:306: lock distance = clamp(15.5+0.6d, 17, 28), i.e. ~17 m, CLOSER than exploration's 24 m. At 17 m and pitch 47 only ~5 m of ground behind Kaito is on screen, so the ninja Estocada (lunge 3.2 m from up to 5.5 m) can start off-screen.

CameraDirector.cs:311: lock yaw ±9°. MovementBasis (line 86) uses that yaw, so stick directions drift while circling a target.

Punch() (line 112) sets fovPunch = delta instantly, an instant FOV snap on a 30° FOV:
- perfect parry -6 (-20%)
- parry -3.5
- dash +2.5
- finisher -7
- rage -5
- kill -3

The duration argument is ignored.

No off-screen indicator exists. UpdateOccluders (line 346) only clears the line to Kaito, so enemies under canopies or roofs stay hidden, and ShadowsOnly keeps the occluder's shadow over Kaito.

Boss framing: focus only 27% toward a boss at 7 m (line 317); in boss_goro3.png Gorō sits under the HUD corner.
issues.fix:
Values:
- exploreDistance 24 → 22, explorePitch 52 → 50
- combatPitch 47 → 44
- lock targetDist = clamp(18 + 0.5d, 19, 25), never closer than 19
- remove lock yaw (or ≤3° and keep MovementBasis on zoneYaw)
- boss: focus weight 0.45 toward the boss, +2 m

Punch → impulse: fovPunchVel += delta*14, clamp |fovPunch| ≤ 3°. Values: parry -1.5, perfect -3, kill -1.5, dash 0 (use speed lines).

Off-screen threat chevrons (UI world layer, screen edge) for token holders outside the viewport, colored by kind, pulsing when strikeEta < cueLead.

Occlusion: also sphere-cast to LockTarget and token holders; replace ShadowsOnly with a dithered fade (keep shading, drop its shadow while hidden).

issues.title: Unblockables require a dash, but the dash requires 15 Spirit: unanswerable attacks
issues.evidence:
PlayerConfig.cs:59 dashCost 15. TryDash → SpendSpirit (Combat.cs:300) → denied sound and shake when short. DamageInfo.CanBeParried excludes Unblockable (CombatTypes.cs).

The sumo charge runs at 11 m/s with 30 damage; Gorō slam 38-42 damage in r 4.6-6 m; Ōzeki charge 13 m/s; Kage windslash 30 damage. Kaito runs at 6.2 m/s, so outrunning is impossible.

Spirit is also the finisher (30) and ability (30-35) currency, so a player who spends it correctly is then defenceless against the next unblockable.
issues.fix:
Choose one:
(a) Allow a 'tired dash' when Spirit < dashCost: same i-frames, distance 4.5 m, 1.2 s cooldown, no perfect-dodge refund or rage, a grey trail.
(b) In-combat Spirit regen of +3/s up to a floor of 15.

Option (a) also keeps dash readable in the HUD.

issues.title: Group AI fairness: clumping, 0.6 s token gap, counters bypass tokens, attacks right after the finisher cinematic
issues.evidence:
CombatDirector.cs:43-46: maxAttackers 2 with only 0.6 s between grants. Ninja a1→a2 is ~0.57 s apart, so two attackers' strikes interleave at ~0.3-0.6 s.

Enemy.cs:412 `if (counter) Game.Combat?.RequestAttackToken(this);` ignores the result, so a counter can be a third simultaneous attacker.

Strafe (Enemy.cs:337-355) has no separation. Enemies keep their approach angle and stack (darkness_lift_demo.png: three ninjas in a ~1.5 m clump, their HP bars and texts overlapping in finisher_prompt.png).

During Kaito's ~2.6 s finisher, other enemies keep running patterns, and IsInvulnerable ends with the state (PlayerController.cs:398), so control often returns mid-enemy-swing.
issues.fix:
CombatDirector.RequestAttackToken:
- gap 0.6 → 1.0 s
- deny when any current attacker has StrikeEta < 0.6 s
- Counter: if the token is denied, EnterGuard instead of attacking

Add angular slots: assign each engaged non-attacker a slot angle spaced 360/n (min 70°) around Kaito and use it as the Strafe destination.

After a finisher or execution:
- invulnUntil = now + 0.6 s
- Push enemies within 4 m by 1.5 m
- their nextAttackTime += 0.8 s; release tokens

issues.title: Boss fights: phase change breaks lock-on, silently ignores hits, wipes posture; boss posture invisible
issues.evidence:
Boss.cs:107-108 PhaseChange: SetState(Scripted) and Imbalance = 0.
- Enemy.Targetable is false while Scripted (Enemy.cs:30), so PlayerController.UpdateTargeting drops or switches the lock (PlayerController.cs:263-270) at every phase threshold and the camera reframes.
- ReceiveHit returns Ignored while Scripted (Enemy.cs:603), so for 1.1 s Kaito's hits produce no flash, no sound, nothing.
- A boss one parry from exhaustion has its progress wiped.

UIManager.cs:301/305/397 exclude bosses from imbalance pips. The boss bar only blinks gold while exhausted (UIManager.cs:226), so in a boss fight the player has no idea how close the boss is to breaking. maxImbalance: Gorō 4, Mizuchi 5, Kage 5.
issues.fix:
- Replace the Scripted state in PhaseChange with an 'Invulnerable/Roaring' flag that keeps Targetable true. Hits during the roar answer with clang, sparks and a 0.05 s hit-stop.
- Defer PhaseChange while Exhausted, until exhaustion ends.
- Keep Imbalance across phases.
- Add posture pips (or a thin posture bar that fills toward the center) under the boss HP bar in UIManager.BuildBossBar / UpdateBossBar.

issues.title: Death/retry loop is long: 6.4 s death sequence, 75-91 m runbacks, unskippable boss intro each attempt, manual checkpoints
issues.evidence:
StoryDirector.DeathRoutine: 1.4 s + DeathScreen (1.2 + 1.6 + 0.6 s, UIManager.Panels) + 0.4 + 1.2 s fade-in ≈ 6.4 s.

Nearest checkpoint to each boss (world_plan.py:210-221 vs 249-253):
- Mizuchi arena (184,72) ← cp_lake_docks (112,16): 91 m straight-line, more along the boardwalks
- Ōzeki (124,162) ← cp_bamboo (72,108): 75 m

BossArena.Update re-runs StoryDirector.BossIntroRoutine on every attempt: 0.8 + 2.6 s fixed waits plus intro dialogue (Areas.cs:207-216).

Checkpoints only register when the player prays (Checkpoint.Interact, Interactables.cs:100). A player who skips praying respawns even further back.
issues.fix:
- Death sequence ≈3.3 s: slow-mo 1.0, panel fade 0.6, hold 0.6, fade 0.3, fade-in 0.8.
- Auto-register the respawn point on proximity (6 m); praying heals and saves.
- Add checkpoints at the Mizuchi arena entrance (boardwalk ≈(172,60)) and the Ōzeki arena entrance (≈(114,150)).
- Flag boss_seen_<id>: on later attempts, a 1.2 s re-intro shot with no dialogue.
- Optional: 'Reintentar jefe' on the death screen.

issues.title: Slow-motion and flash overuse dilute impact and hide the next attack
issues.evidence:
Slow-mo sources:
- every non-finisher kill: 0.3 for 0.35 s (Combat.cs:188)
- perfect parry: 0.3 for 0.45 s plus chromatic aberration
- finisher: 0.45 for 1.6 s
- rage: 0.35 for 0.45 s
- finisher tip: 0.25 for 1.2 s
- boss phase: 0.4 for 0.7 s

In a 3-ninja fight a large share of the time runs in slow-motion, and ScreenFX desaturates by 45×(1-scale).

The perfect-parry flash is flashGold 2.6 × 1.8 = 4.7 m additive sprite, plus a 3.5 m ring, plus VFX, plus a 10-intensity light (FXManager.cs:50, 132-134). In finisher_prompt2.png it whites out both fighters, hiding the follow-up swing.
issues.fix:
- Kill slow-mo only on the last enemy of an encounter, or for a double kill within 1 s; otherwise a 0.06 s global hit-stop.
- Perfect-parry slow-mo only when it breaks posture (Imbalance reaches max); otherwise a 0.09 s hit-stop plus a flash.
- Parry flash scale: perfect 1.8 → 1.0, normal 1.1 → 0.7, lifetime ≤ 0.1 s, offset to the blade-contact point.
- Finisher-tip slow-mo only the first time (already flagged).

issues.title: Light-hit feedback is almost invisible camera-wise; Kaito and enemies slide during hit-stop
issues.evidence:
Light hits call Shake(0.18). Shake = trauma² × 2.6° = 0.08° and 0.011 m (CameraDirector.cs:268-276). Impulse peaks ~0.06 m at 24 m distance. There is no global hit-stop on non-kill hits, only a local anim Freeze of 0.06 s (Combat.cs:156-157).

During Freeze, attackNorm stops (Combat.cs:45) but the lunge velocity keeps being applied (Combat.cs:52-65). Kaito glides ~0.3 m as a frozen statue. Same for the enemy lunge (Enemy.cs:469-474).

The player has no HitFlash when hurt.
issues.fix:
- First connecting hit of each swing: Game.Time.HitStop(0.035) on light hits and 0.07 on heavy.

issues.title: Tutorials teach an invisible cue; the first sumo/dash tutorial is a 3-enemy fight; automated tests validate superhuman parries
issues.evidence:
StoryDirector.cs:252-265 freezes the world at AboutToStrike (StrikeEta ≤ 0.18 s) and shows '¡AHORA!'. At full speed nothing visible happens at that moment, so the lesson doesn't transfer. The tutorial ends after 3 tries with no real-time practice.

The dash is unlocked at the first unblockable anywhere. The 'sumo' encounter (world_plan.py:239) is sumo plus 2 ninjas, and boss_goro3.png shows the dash tutorial triggering mid-Gorō fight for players who went to the mountain first.

AutoPilot.cs:133-141 parries on AboutToStrike with zero reaction time, so automated runs report successful parries the cue timing can't support for humans.
issues.fix:
- Tutorial: freeze at the tell (strikeEta ≤ cueLead) and highlight the gold rim/ring with 'Cuando brilla en dorado, presioná [K]'. Then require 2 real-time successes, optionally with a 0.6× slow-mo assist on the first.
- Intro ninja: single-step patterns with cueLead 0.6 s.
- Spawn the sumo encounter's 2 ninjas only when the sumo's HP drops below 60%.
- Show the dash tutorial on a guaranteed sumo, not a boss.
- AutoPilot: press parry at tell time + 0.25 ± 0.04 s instead of StrikeEta, so tests fail when cue lead < reaction time.

issues.title: Input feel: dead lock-on taps, momentum killed on attack, combo restart lag
issues.evidence:
Lock-on tap (PlayerController.cs:276-289): with a single target, CycleTarget returns the same enemy and nothing happens. Release needs a 0.45 s hold (line 274), so the tap feels broken.

StartAttack sets velocity = 0 (Combat.cs:35), so running into an attack stops dead.

After Attack3 the state only returns to Locomotion after comboGrace 0.25 s (Combat.cs:96-109), while the attack buffer is 0.2 s (PlayerController.cs:197). Presses while mashing are lost and the restart feels sticky.
issues.fix:
- Lock: tap with ≤1 valid target releases the lock; tap with more cycles; hold stays as release.
- StartAttack: keep 35% of the run velocity, blended into the lunge.
- After the last combo step: allow StartAttack(0) from attackNorm ≥ 0.85 with a 0.3 s buffer.

issues.title: Per-event allocations and heavy defaults (minor perf/GC risks)
issues.evidence:
FXManager says 'nothing is instantiated in combat', yet:
- RingWave.Spawn and SlashLineFX.Spawn create a new GameObject per parry/shockwave/slash (FXFactory.cs:272, 330)
- UIManager.AddMarker creates a new TMP object plus an outline material per '!', '危', '防' (UIManager.cs:385-392)
- HitFlash.Flash allocates new Material[] per renderer per hit (CharacterFX.cs:203-216)
- AfterImages allocate a WaitForSeconds per tick

Standalone default quality is Ultra (QualitySettings m_PerPlatformDefaultQuality Standalone: 5): 4096 soft shadows, 2 cascades, 70 m, plus DOF, bloom and SMAA, alongside 10 pooled pixel lights and 4 flash lights.
issues.fix:
- Pool RingWave, SlashLine and the marker texts.
- HitFlash via MaterialPropertyBlock (emission/flash color), not material swaps.
- Cache the WaitForSeconds.
- Standalone default 'High' (2048 shadows) with Ultra as an option; profile on a student laptop.

plan:
ORDER = highest game-feel return first. Steps 1-7 do not depend on the new animations; animators should still meet the GF-03 criteria.

PHASE 1: Parry cue that a human can react to (GF-01, GF-04)
1. Combat/CombatTypes.cs AttackDef: add `public float cueLead = -1f;` (−1 = auto by kind: Light 0.45 s, Heavy 0.55 s, Projectile 0.5 s, Unblockable = start of step) and `public bool followUp;`.
   - EnemyArchetypes.Hit(): set followUp for steps ≥2 of combos (cueLead 0.40).
2. Enemies/Enemy.cs
   - BeginStep: compute natural windup with EstimateStrikeEta at stepNorm 0. If windup < cueLead + 0.10, set a runtime `extraHold` (seconds) so that cue→impact == cueLead.
   - TickAttack:
     - Replace the hold with `holdStart` (set when stepNorm first ≥ activeStart−0.12): `holding = (telegraph+extraHold) > 0 && stepNorm >= activeStart-0.12 && stateTime-holdStart < telegraph+extraHold`.
     - Update EstimateStrikeEta to the same model.
     - Replace line 461 with `if (!telegraphed && strikeEta <= Lead(a))`, which calls `OnStrikeTell(a)` (FX.ParryTell + Audio 'tell_parry'/'tell_heavy').
     - Play a.sfx (whoosh) when strikeEta <= 0.12.
     - Add `public float TellLead` used by tutorials and AutoPilot.
3. FX/FXManager.cs: new `ParryTell(Enemy e, AttackKind k, float lead)`:
   (a) full-body rim flash 0.15 s: gold (1,0.82,0.35) for parryable, red (1,0.2,0.15) for unblockable, via a MaterialPropertyBlock on the rim shader (Phase 2) or HitFlash with a tinted material as a fallback;
   (b) head/eye glint sprite 0.6 m, 0.25 s;
   (c) 'closing ring' under Kaito, the RingWave variant shrinking 2.2 → 0.6 m over `lead`, oriented with a notch toward the attacker. Only token holders, max 2.
   - BladeGlint lifetime 0.09 → 0.2 s, scale ×2.

PHASE 3: Combat loop rules (GF-05, GF-06, GF-09, GF-13, GF-14)

   - EnemyArchetypes: ninja poiseHits 2 → 3, elite 1 → 2.
